title: His father's advice, wool underwear and Art Graham
summary: His father gives advice and long underwear for North Dakota; Thomas reads piano parts on C-melody, and Art Graham from St. Paul joins and outplays him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What did you do? How did you get out there? By car?

He had a Ford car. And I remember... Now, the first thing when I went out there, my father sit down and talk to me, told me about life. I often wondered how he knew all that jazz. But I followed his advice. So he gave me about four or five pair of wool underwear...some of them was wool and silk long underwear. Well, in Oklahoma the temperature was so (?), so you didn't need no long underwear.

Well, when I got out there, I needed it. So... Because I got out there in like July or August, and I got in the band... I could play. I could play good enough to play with this band. Because I could play all the popular tunes of
that day, and then the new songs, they'd bring in a piano part and I'd just read it... That was one thing about the C-melody; you'd just read the notes that's on there.
And.... Art Graham is that boy's name. And I guess the band got a little bigger, because they sent for Art Graham. He was from St. Paul. And Art played up a beast(?), man. He was good. He played...
That's quite a little ways, isn't it.

He played better than I did. Well, see, them guys would... You'd send them a ticket. Because he sent me my ticket! I'm all the way down in Tulsa. I said, "Send me a ticket and I'll go." He sent me a ticket...
He bought you a ticket from Tulsa to where?
That's how I first got out in that Midwest. Because I remember...
All that was still wide-open country.
